name: The Last Slice
blurb: Three flatmates, one slice of pizza, and a politeness contest nobody wants to lose
title: The Last Slice: 30-Second Comedy Skit Script for 3
description: A 30-second vertical comedy script for 3 flatmates: one pizza slice left and everyone politely pretends not to want it. Free to film and perform.
h1: The Last Slice: a 30-Second Comedy Script for 3 People
logline: One slice of pizza is left in the box, and three hungry flatmates would rather starve than look greedy. Each offer is more polite than the last, until the lights go out.
setting: A small kitchen or living room at night. Props: an open pizza box with one slice (any flat bread works), a knife, three phones with torches.

roles.name: Rosa
roles.note: Any gender, 18+. The one who paid. Wants the slice most, hides it best.

roles.name: Kai
roles.note: Any gender, 18+. Over-polite, tries to win with compliments.

roles.name: Noor
roles.note: Any gender, 18+. The dramatic one. Claims to be full.

script.action: An open pizza box. One slice left. Three flatmates stare at it.

script.say: Kai, you're still growing. It's yours.
I'd be happiest just watching you two eat it.

script.action: Nobody moves. All three fake a yawn and leave in different directions.
Darkness. Three phone torches creep back in and meet over the box.
Rosa cuts the slice into three thin pieces. They chew, very satisfied.

head: Shot
What we see / hear
Seconds
rows: The box with one slice, three faces lean in
You have it, no you have it, I'm so full
Stomach growl, Noor blames the fridge
Kai and Rosa's offers, Noor's speech
Fake yawns, they leave, lights off
Three torches meet over the box, Kai whispers
Three thin pieces, the crust question, all three answer

body: Film vertical 9:16 from the end of the table so all three faces fit in one frame; the top-down shot of the box is the hook, so make it the first frame. For the dark scene, switch off the room light and let the three phone torches light the faces from below, which reads funny rather than scary. Record a real stomach growl or add one in editing. Two or three takes are usually enough; the last line needs perfect timing, so do it a few extra times.

ul: Everyone must look hungry while saying they are not. The joke lives in the eyes, not the words.
Each offer is more generous than the one before. Noor's line should feel like an acceptance speech.
After the stomach growl, hold a beat of silence before Noor blames the fridge.
In the dark, move slowly and freeze when the torches meet. Kai's whisper should sound guilty.
Rehearse the last line until all three say it at exactly the same moment. If it overlaps badly, it loses the laugh.
Swap the pizza for the last dumpling, the last piece of cake at an office party, or the last cookie in a tin.
Play it with two people for a tighter duel, or with four or five for a bigger politeness war.
Different ending: when the torches meet, the box is already empty, and a fourth flatmate is heard chewing in the dark.

prompts.keyframe: Top-down view of an open pizza box with a single slice left on a kitchen table, three young adults lean in from three sides staring at it, warm overhead light, comic tension, cinematic still, vertical 9:16.
shots: Slow pan across three flatmates at a kitchen table, each politely gestures at a single pizza slice for the others to take, exaggerated smiles, warm light, comedy mood, vertical 9:16.
Wide shot of a dark kitchen, three phone torches creep in from three doorways and meet above a pizza box, faces lit from below, sneaky comic mood, vertical 9:16.
Close-up of a knife cutting one slice of pizza into three thin pieces, then pull back to three flatmates chewing happily, warm light, comedy, vertical 9:16.

faq.q: Can I use this script for a school club or a competition?
faq.a: Yes. It is free under CC BY 4.0 for any use, including competitions and paid events. Credit "Script: cv.cm" in your programme or video description.

faq.q: Can two people do it instead of three?
faq.a: Yes. Give Noor's lines to Rosa and Kai, and keep the stomach growl and the fridge excuse. The ending still works: two voices saying you have it at the same time.

faq.q: How long does it take to shoot?
faq.a: About half an hour with one or two run-throughs. The whole sketch runs 30 seconds, so rehearse it start to finish three times before filming.
